hook: Phosphorus next to a nickel single-atom catalyst steers deuterium onto haloanilines at chosen sites.
summary: Adding phosphorus outside the nickel's main coordination shell lets the catalyst grab the amino group of haloanilines and swap in deuterium from D2O and H2 at specific positions, leaving carbon-halogen bonds intact. A phosphorus-free version is nearly inactive. Evidence is spectroscopy and calculation on a few aniline substrates.
title: Functional Specialization of Coordination Spheres Enables Site-Selective Aromatic C–H Isotope Exchange in Ni Single-Atom Catalysts
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
